weekly:10.22827/seoul.2020..106.004.caption:
How old is Seoul's Tram 381?

Hwang Haejin revisits a familiar museum object: Tram 381, preserved at the Seoul Museum of History. The study challenges its conventional dating to the 1930s, arguing instead that it was made in 1944–45 at a Nippon Sharyo factory in Incheon.

How can a historian establish an object's age when its history is uncertain? Hwang compares vehicle types, technical drawings, company records and contemporary newspapers. The tram's semi-steel construction provides an initial clue: this type entered Gyeongseong, colonial Seoul, no earlier than 1929.

The numbering system then narrows the possibilities. Company records identify No. 335 as the latest comparable vehicle in 1939. Hwang establishes that numbers were assigned within vehicle categories in acquisition order, making No. 381 later than that benchmark. Records from the 1940s support the final 1944–45 estimate.

The argument turns a question about one tram into a lesson in historical method: a number becomes evidence only when we understand the system that produced it. Looking closely at an everyday object can unsettle an apparently settled chronology.

황해진 (2020), 「서울역사박물관 소장 전차 ‘381호’ 제작 연대 및 제작지 검토」 [Dating and Locating the Manufacture of Tram 381], 서울과 역사 106, 149–178.
